knowledge_point.title: Calculating Indefinite Integrals Using Substitution with Inverse Tangent

question.:question/worked-solution:
This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse tangent,

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\text{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have $9{x}^{2}=(3x)^{2}.$

So. let's substitute $u=3x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3}{1+9{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{1+(3x)^{2}}\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\cdot (\frac{1}{3}\text{d}u) \\  & =\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C \\  & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3x)+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{9+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{9\cdot (1+{x}^{2}/9)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\int \frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}/9}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\int \frac{1}{1+(x/3)^{2}}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse tangent

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\text{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have ${(\frac{x}{3})}^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{x}{3}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{3}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=3\,\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{9+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{9}\int \frac{1}{1+(x/3)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{9}\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\cdot (3\,\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{\text{d}u}{1+{u}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{3})+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{8}{16+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{8}{16\cdot (1+{x}^{2}/16)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}/16}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{1+(x/4)^{2}}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

This integral resembles the basic integral for inverse tangent

$$
\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\text{d}u=\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C.
$$

The only difference is that instead of ${u}^{2}$ as the variable, we have ${(\frac{x}{4})}^{2}.$

So, let's substitute $u=\frac{x}{4}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{4}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=4\,\text{d}u.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{8}{16+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{1+(x/4)^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{1}{1+{u}^{2}}\cdot (4\,\text{d}u) \\  & =2\int \frac{\text{d}u}{1+{u}^{2}} \\  & =2\operatorname{arctan}⁡u+C \\  & =2\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{x}{4})+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
